newsitem.title: USA: CSX Corp sells $2.25 bln in debt - sources.
newsitem.headline: CSX Corp sells $2.25 bln in debt - sources.

text.p: CSX Corp sold at least $2.25 billion in debt in a 144a offering via Salomon Brothers Inc on Thursday, according to market sources.

The company is rumored to have privately placed additional tranches of 30-year debt, putable in five years, and 35-year debt, callable in 10 years. The final size of the privately placed tranches was not available but sources said the total offering may have been as large as $2.5 billion.
A CSX spokesman and Salomon Brothers officials declined to comment.
CSX will use the proceeds from the offering to finance the purchase of 42 percent of the assets of Conrail Inc for $4.3 billion, a CSX official said.
Norfolk Southern Corp will purchase the remainder of Conrail's assets for $5.9 billion according to an agreement between Conrail and Norfolk Southern announced in April.
The CSX debt offering on Thursday was structured as follows:
*$350 million in 7.05 percent five-year debt priced at 99.935
to yield 7.066 percent *$300 million in 7.25 percent seven-year debt priced at 99.98
to yield 7.254 percent *$450 million in 7.45 percent 10-year debt at 99.849 to yield
7.472 percent *$250 million in 7.25 percent 30-year debt, putable in eight
years at 99.751 to yield 7.292 percent *$400 million in 7.90 percent 20-year debt at 99.942 to yield
7.906 percent *$500 million in 7.95 percent 30-year debt at 99.482 to yield
